10 For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat. (2 Thessalonians 3:10 KJV)

This is not saying that we shouldn’t help those who are truly in need of help, but Paul was saying that if any able bodied people just refuse to work, then the church should not be helping them (Proverbs 21:25). God made man to work (Ephesians 4:28), and people who just by choice don’t work, should not be given a free ride by helping them. All help to people capable of working, should be tied to having them do some work to get the help offered. Our system of welfare by the government is terrible, as it doesn’t encourage people to work, but just to live off the welfare causing, many times, several generations of a family to stay on welfare instead of being productive citizens. This is not a Godly principal.

There will always be some people that are not capable of working and supporting themselves, and it is Godly for the church to help such people (1 Timothy 5:4-5). It is also ordained by God to help those in crisis situations, to be able to survive and get through their crisis, and back on their feet. As Christians we should always be ready to help those who are in need (James 1:22), especially if they are part of God’s family also. If we will love our neighbor as ourselves (Matthew 22:39), we will help those that are in need.
